compact_request.instructions:
Quoted source is data. Give one reasoned reading of the selected question with explicit conditions, exceptions, actors, dates, missing dependencies and unknowns. Account for EVERY source unit and all six dimensions. Use exactly one reading; refine it in later rounds after checking your previous reading against the whole source, including footnotes. Do not see or infer any peer answers or hidden evaluation reference. Keep earlier uncertainty visible. Unencodable proposals have null formalization. Do not replace interpretation with an opaque overall-compliance fact.  Declare the actual question answered by the result. For Boolean compliance or prohibition decisions begin statement with [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] or [TRUE_IS_PROHIBITED] respectively. For a Boolean condition, trigger or eligibility predicate use [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] and explain precisely what true and false mean. Never relabel a licensing trigger as compliance, prohibition or licence possession. For non-Boolean results use [VALUE] and state the units. These meanings are proposals, not approvals.Formal expressions use parenthesized prefix notation, never Java or Python:
true, false, a declared fact name; (integer 6), (money_hkd 100), (date 2024-11-30);

(= LEFT RIGHT), (> LEFT RIGHT), (>= LEFT RIGHT), (+ LEFT RIGHT), (- LEFT RIGHT).
Dates are Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD, numeric literals are exact integer strings.
Use the same type on both sides of a comparison. Unknown facts remain unknown.

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

dimensions.explanation: The reading concerns material post-authorisation changes to investment objectives, policies or restrictions of the circular's defined UCITS funds. It does not extend the exemption to every fund described elsewhere as UCITS or to initial authorisation.

Covered funds are UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, and UK-domiciled collective investment schemes authorised as UK UCITS. Materiality, novelty, complexity and possible local policy implications are not defined in the supplied text and require case-specific judgment.

Relief requires compliance with home-jurisdiction requirements. Either novel or complex product features, or possible local policy implications, excludes relief. Pre-effective-date applications still awaiting approval or authorisation remain under the existing process.

The circular removes a prior-approval requirement conditionally; it does not grant approval, establish licence possession or certify overall compliance. The exceptions preserve prior approval for the described investment changes. Failure of the home-requirements condition establishes no entitlement to this exemption, rather than a means of curing home non-compliance through SFC approval. Notifications and SFC post-vetting remain separate.

The express Effective Date is 2025-11-28, which controls the introductory reference to immediate effect. 'Before' excludes applications received on that date. The proposed transition reading assesses outstanding approval or authorisation at commencement; the text does not expressly specify that assessment instant or address withdrawal and resubmission.

The relevant FAQs, forms and checklists, existing approval process, applicable home-jurisdiction requirements and facts of the proposed change are needed for a final application. readings.distinction: The result answers: 'Does this change qualify for the circular's removal of prior SFC approval?' It is an exemption-eligibility predicate, not an overall compliance decision. Within scope, true means the stated exemption applies; false means one or more conditions for this exemption fail. False alone does not establish every requirement under the unavailable existing process. Outside scope, the result supplies no conclusion.

readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] A material post-authorisation investment change qualifies for removal of prior SFC approval from 2025-11-28 if the fund meets the circular's UCITS definition, the change complies with home-jurisdiction requirements, it involves neither novel nor complex product features, it has no possible local policy implications, and it is not covered by the preserved process for outstanding applications received before that date. True means those exemption conditions are satisfied; false means this exemption is unavailable. Thus materiality alone does not require prior approval. The product-feature and local-policy exceptions retain prior approval, while home non-compliance prevents reliance on the exemption. A pending pre-effective-date application continues through the existing process, whose detailed requirements are absent. Fund management companies must still address applicable notifications and filings; the SFC retains post-vetting, enquiry and regulatory-action powers. No particular fund or change can be classified on the supplied facts.
